title: TrumpFile: a Czechoslovak informant makes an unsupported tax claim about Trump
description_medium: Czechoslovak state-security files show that the StB monitored Donald Trump and Ivana Trump during the 1970s and 1980s. A 1977 informant said Trump’s businesses were “completely tax-exempt for the next 30 years,” but the Guardian does not verify that claim. Separate tax reporting cited by the article said a large business loss could offset Trump’s income for up to 18 years.
description_long: The Guardian reviewed Czechoslovak state-security files showing that the StB collected information about Donald Trump and his wife Ivana during the 1970s and 1980s. In a 1977 report, an informant using the cover name Lubos said Trump’s businesses were safe because they received state commissions, and claimed Trump was “completely tax-exempt for the next 30 years.” The Guardian does not say the StB verified this statement. It separately reports that the New York Times reviewed Trump tax records showing he could have used a $916 million loss reported in 1995 to avoid income tax for up to 18 years. That later tax finding does not validate the informant’s claim. The file documents surveillance and an informant’s statement, not a legal tax exemption through 2007.

corrected_wording.proposed: Czechoslovak intelligence files include an informant’s unsupported claim about Trump’s tax status
corrected_wording.reason: The Guardian reports an informant’s statement from an intelligence file, not a verified tax exemption.

source_access_notes: The Guardian article was read directly.
blockers: The StB file records the informant’s claim but does not provide its basis or establish Trump’s actual tax status.
rationale: The Guardian distinguishes the informant’s 1977 assertion from later tax-record reporting; this wording preserves that distinction and avoids treating surveillance notes as a tax determination.

title: Wayne Barrett reports a 1979 bribery inquiry involving Trump
description_medium: Donald Trump biographer Wayne Barrett wrote that Trump was the subject of a bribery investigation in mid-1979. TrumpFile attributes the claim to Barrett’s 1992 book, but the linked account does not identify the investigating agency, describe the alleged conduct or report how the inquiry ended.
description_long: In his 1992 biography Trump: The Deals and the Downfall, journalist Wayne Barrett wrote that Donald Trump was the subject of a bribery investigation in mid-1979. TrumpFile’s timeline repeats the claim and cites Barrett’s book. The available account does not identify the agency, explain what alleged payment or official action was involved, or say whether investigators closed the inquiry, referred it for prosecution or reached any conclusion. It is therefore a report about an alleged investigation, not a finding that Trump committed bribery. The source also does not substantiate the title’s suggestion of possible mob ties as part of this particular inquiry.

corrected_wording.proposed: Wayne Barrett reports a 1979 bribery inquiry involving Trump
corrected_wording.reason: The title frames a biographer-reported inquiry as an established fact and implies mob ties without independent records.

source_access_notes: TrumpFile’s linked account and cited Barrett attribution were read; no underlying agency record was available.
blockers: The source does not identify the investigating agency, the alleged bribe or the inquiry’s disposition; no contemporaneous investigative record is supplied.
rationale: The available source traces the 1979 inquiry claim to Barrett’s retrospective biography; absent agency, conduct and outcome, the text attributes rather than asserts the allegation.
